findings.description: The harness satisfies every bullet in B-4's list, and the two-sided baseline control behaves on both halves, each against its own freshly built repo.
findings.evidence:
I extracted the shipped harness verbatim (tests/sync.bats:24-118) into a control file outside the repo and ran the baseline script `git show 298c8a6:dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync` under it, unmodified.
POSITIVE half, case A1 (detached, dirty), pre-run porcelain `[?? change.txt]`, count 1 -> reaches the commit phase:
  ==> Committing 1 file
  [detached HEAD 402e283] [auto-sync from That-Air] 2026-01-01 - 1 file
  STATUS: 0 / AFTER count: 2
NEGATIVE half, case A2 (detached, clean), pre-run porcelain `[]`, count 1:
  ==> Nothing to commit. Already in sync.
  STATUS: 0 / AFTER count: 1
Separate repos per half (BATS_TEST_TMPDIR .../test/1/repo vs .../test/2/repo). Baseline confirmed guard-free: `grep -c 'Refusing to commit' baseline-sync` = 0, clean-tree exit at baseline :130-133.
Stub contract, item by item, from a harness-audit probe printing the live environment:
  PATH=/var/.../test/3/stubs:/usr/bin:/bin  -- authoritative, not prepended; byte-identical to tests/apps.bats:73 (`export PATH="$STUBS:/usr/bin:/bin"`), not tests/doctor.bats:62 (`export PATH="$STUBS:$PATH"`). Artifact line is tests/sync.bats:48.
  code/brew/jq/claude-plugins-capture/claude-settings-normalize -> ABSENT (all five), and the run printed each phase's documented skip branch: 'code CLI not found, skipping', 'claude-plugins-capture not found, skipping', 'claude-settings-normalize not found, skipping', 'brew or jq not found, skipping'.
  chezmoi -> stub. `chezmoi source-path` (no args) -> the scratch repo path; `chezmoi source-path /some/path` -> non-zero (drift loop takes its `|| continue` at :90); `chezmoi status` -> empty `[]`; `re-add` -> exit 0 (tests/sync.bats:69-73), and the run passed :66 without aborting.
  date -u +%Y-%m-%d -> 2026-01-01, and that token appears in the commit subject above, so it is pinned at the source.
  osascript records the FULL argument list, not just that it ran: OSA_LOG contents `[-e display notification "b" with title "Dotfiles sync failed"]` (tests/sync.bats:87-90, `printf '%s\n' "$*"`).
  DOTFILES_AUTO_PUSH -> UNSET (tests/sync.bats:35), and the run took the opt-in branch at :182 printing 'Auto-push is off; push manually'.
  HOME -> /var/.../test/3/home, redirected (tests/sync.bats:32).
  $STUBS and $HOME are OUTSIDE the scratch repo: REPO=.../test/3/repo, STUBS=.../test/3/stubs, HOME=.../test/3/home are siblings under BATS_TEST_TMPDIR, and a freshly built repo's porcelain reads `[]` (empty), so the clean/dirty axis is intact.
  fresh_repo builds a bare origin and pushes to it (tests/sync.bats:107-118), verified by the control run completing `git push -q origin main` without error.

findings.description: Independent ruling on the flagged judgment call: the worker's reading is CORRECT -- B-4's two-sided baseline control is the checker's own probe, not a case the worker had to commit. No defect.
findings.evidence:
Ruled from clause text, not inherited from the worker. Four independent supports:
(1) B-4 (constitution.md:199) places the control 'before any V-1 case' and makes it gate their meaning -- 'If either half misbehaves the harness is broken and every V-1 result afterward is meaningless.' V-1 (constitution.md:120) states its nine cases are 'the checker's own. It may not be delegated to the worker's bats file.' A control whose job is to validate the checker's probe run before it starts belongs to that run.
(2) The control requires the baseline at 298c8a6, which is not in the working tree and must be `git show`n to a temp path -- the same extraction V-4 (constitution.md:143) assigns to the checker.
(3) B-3 (constitution.md:181) is the clause that governs what must be COMMITTED, and it enumerates its list exhaustively -- 'all four of: a case driving the attached, no-operation path...; a detached-HEAD case; a rebase-in-progress case; and a merge-in-progress case.' The control is not among them, and revision 7 rewrote B-3 precisely to name committed requirements explicitly rather than leave them implied.
(4) T-002's own check_method (.agent-guild/state/tasks/T-002.md:10-14) says so directly: 'B-4 is a procedure the checker verifies by running: build the harness this task ships, run the baseline script at 298c8a6 under it, and confirm the two-sided control behaves.'
One correction to the worker's stated reasoning, which does not change the outcome: the analogy to V-1's 'probe is the checker's own' sentence is imprecise, since that sentence is scoped to V-1 rather than to B-4. The conclusion stands on B-4's and B-3's own text plus the check_method above.
What the clause does require of the worker is a harness CAPABLE of carrying the control, and I verified that operationally: the control ran on tests/sync.bats:24-118 extracted verbatim, with zero modifications to the harness.

findings.description: Every case drives the real script against a throwaway repo, nothing reimplements the guard, and no path reaches the real ~/.local/share/chezmoi even if a stub failed to take effect.
findings.evidence:
Each of the four cases invokes the real script: `run bash "$SCRIPT"` at tests/sync.bats:124, 139, 155, 174, with SCRIPT="$SRC/dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync" (tests/sync.bats:25). The file contains no reimplementation of the guard -- the only guard strings in it are the three expected-message constants at tests/sync.bats:27-29, used as assert_contains/assert_not_contains needles, never as logic. This is corroborated behaviorally: all three per-detector mutations of the real script flipped the corresponding case (see B-3), which is impossible if the cases were asserting against a copy.
Reachability of the real source dir: the script derives SRC from `chezmoi source-path` at :18 and only then `cd "$SRC"` at :128. Under the authoritative PATH the stub is what answers; if the stub failed to take effect there is no fallback, because the real binary is at /opt/homebrew/bin/chezmoi, which is not on `/usr/bin:/bin`. Probe:
  $ env -i HOME=... PATH="/usr/bin:/bin" /bin/bash dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync
  dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync: line 18: chezmoi: command not found
The run dies at :18 under `set -euo pipefail` (:16), before `cd "$SRC"` and before any git command, so a failed stub aborts rather than falling through to the real source dir.
The test file's own SRC (tests/sync.bats:24, "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/..") is used solely to locate the script; it is not exported, so the child `bash "$SCRIPT"` does not inherit it, and the script assigns its own SRC at :18 unconditionally in any case. Nothing in the file derives a path from an unstubbed `chezmoi source-path`.

findings.description: All four committed cases are present, the merge marker is built with `git rev-parse HEAD > .git/MERGE_HEAD`, and each case builds its own fresh scratch repo.
findings.evidence:
Four @test blocks in tests/sync.bats, one per required case:
  :120 'sync: attached branch with no operation in progress commits normally' -- the attached, no-operation path, asserting the run commits: `[ "$status" -eq 0 ]`, assert_contains "Committed locally", and rev-list count 1 -> 2 (:126-129).
  :132 detached HEAD (`git -C "$REPO" checkout -q --detach HEAD`, :134).
  :148 rebase in progress (`mkdir -p "$REPO/.git/rebase-merge"`, :150, on an attached HEAD).
  :164 merge in progress, marker built exactly as the clause requires: `git -C "$REPO" rev-parse HEAD >"$REPO/.git/MERGE_HEAD"` (:169), so the file holds a real commit id rather than being empty.
Fresh repo per case: every case calls fresh_repo (:121, :149, :165 and :133), which does `git init -q --bare` plus `git init -q "$REPO"` under $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR (:107-118), a per-@test directory. Proven empirically rather than assumed: the rebase case at :148 mkdir's .git/rebase-merge, and the merge case that runs after it asserts `assert_not_contains "$REBASE_MSG"` (:179) and passes. Under a shared fixture that marker survives `git clean -xdff` and the merge case would report the rebase state, which is the exact failure revision 6 describes. My control run also showed BATS_TEST_TMPDIR differing per test (.../test/1/repo vs .../test/3/repo) on this bats (1.14.0).
Suite as found, before any mutation: `bats tests/sync.bats` -> 1..4, all four ok.

findings.description: Each blocked-state case asserts the specific state string V-2 requires and the absence of the other two families, not merely a non-zero exit.
findings.evidence:
The three family constants are tests/sync.bats:27-29:
  DETACHED_MSG="Refusing to commit: HEAD is detached"
  REBASE_MSG="Refusing to commit: rebase in progress"
  MERGE_MSG="Refusing to commit: merge in progress"
Each matches the script's own refusal text at :140, :144 and :149 respectively.
Detached case, tests/sync.bats:141-145: `[ "$status" -ne 0 ]`, assert_contains "$DETACHED_MSG", assert_not_contains "$REBASE_MSG", assert_not_contains "$MERGE_MSG", plus rev-list count unchanged against a before_count captured at :137.
Rebase case, :157-161: same shape, assert_contains "$REBASE_MSG" with DETACHED and MERGE asserted absent.
Merge case, :176-180: same shape, assert_contains "$MERGE_MSG" with DETACHED and REBASE asserted absent.
So no case rests on `[ "$status" -ne 0 ]` alone, and a guard reporting every state as the same one fails two of the three cases on the absence assertions. The assertion primitives are the pre-existing helpers (tests/helpers.bash assert_contains via `grep -qF`, assert_not_contains via `case`), which propagate failure correctly under bash 3.2 errexit; no new primitive was written.

findings.description: All three per-detector mutations flip exactly the cases covering that detector and leave the others, including the attached case, green. Case-to-mutation mapping recorded below.
findings.evidence:
DIGEST BRACKET, before the first mutation:
  $ shasum -a 256 dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync
  c90191bfb7fa6d48dc7deb5d6bb51fe41cebfa84446816ab206a2410fc04dc73
Restore copy taken to an absolute path outside the repo BEFORE any mutation (<scratch>/dotfiles-sync.RESTORE, same digest), restored with `cp` and verified with `diff` after each mutation. `git checkout` was never used on this file.
CASE-TO-MUTATION MAPPING (script region :138-151 is the if/elif/elif guard):
  Mutation 1, delete ONLY the detached-HEAD detector (script :146-150) -> flips 'sync: detached HEAD refuses...'
    1..4 | ok 1 attached | not ok 2 detached | ok 3 rebase | ok 4 merge
  Mutation 2, delete ONLY the rebase detector (script :138-141, remaining `elif [ -f MERGE_HEAD ]` promoted to `if`) -> flips 'sync: rebase in progress refuses...'
    1..4 | ok 1 attached | ok 2 detached | not ok 3 rebase | ok 4 merge
  Mutation 3, delete ONLY the merge detector (script :142-145) -> flips 'sync: merge in progress refuses...'
    1..4 | ok 1 attached | ok 2 detached | ok 3 rebase | not ok 4 merge
Each mutant passed `bash -n` first, so no case flipped on a syntax error. Exactly one case flips per mutation and the attached case stays green throughout, so each detector is independently load-bearing.
DIGEST BRACKET, after restoring from the last mutation:
  $ diff dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync <scratch>/dotfiles-sync.RESTORE  -> no output (byte-identical)
  $ shasum -a 256 dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync
  c90191bfb7fa6d48dc7deb5d6bb51fe41cebfa84446816ab206a2410fc04dc73
  $ git rev-parse HEAD -> 298c8a69f839b336c248ec1b1b6607b4f43de589
  $ git status --porcelain -> ' M dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync' and '?? tests/sync.bats' (unchanged from start)
Suite green after full restore: `bats tests/` exit 0, `bats --count tests/` = 124 (> 120), cases 121-124 are the four new sync cases; `bats tests/lint.bats` exit 0, 'ok 1 no bare [[ or (( on the guarded surface'. lint.bats's own pattern applied directly to tests/sync.bats returns zero matches (grep exit 1).
